source_en: Going home, as the State requires!
Census route. Every name saves someone!
Home before curfew. Curfew is a gift.
Updating the registry. The State is busy!
Delivering forms. They let me carry them!
Staying indoors, as told. So looked after.
Being counted first. I asked to be!
Perfecting the records. The State is coming.
Going home. Door unlocked, as they asked.
Fetching my husband from the bread factory.
New here. Looking for the housing office.
Paying a fine for filing late.
Moving into a shared flat. I hate being alone.
Census office trainee. Started this week.
Meeting this post's officer. Forgot his name.
Taking my children to the shelter.
The records don't matter. Nobody will save us.
Leaving before they order something worse.
Good evening! The State asked for documents. I was SO happy to bring them.
Every paper correct. I filled them in twice, just for the joy.
Gaps in the registry now. People who did not listen. All to plan.
The radio says not to speculate about the blast. I never need to!
They say the State abandoned us. I have written their names down.
The State knew about the blast long before us. Soon it will explain.
Wonderful! The State thanks you. I will remember your face.
You did as instructed. Look how beautifully it all works!
The State sees your obedience. Does it not feel good?
Writing materials, please. I have so much gratitude to record.
The State put me here. The safest room in the district!
I updated my own entry this morning. The State loves accuracy.
To be given an order is to be loved. I was so loved.
Where are you coming from?
My census route! Every door answered but two. I reported which two.
The district office. Registry corrections, plus everyone who questioned the curfew.
My last addresses. Doors open, as instructed. I recorded what was inside.
The tram depot ticket office. The census forms are just a Sunday hobby.
The district office, explaining why the registry is late. I have been careless.
The western district. I only moved to this town last month.
Are you experiencing any symptoms?
None! I report my health to the office every morning. My favourite part!
Three hours of sleep since the blast. I cannot miss a single broadcast!
None. If I had any, the State would tell me. And I would thank it.
My eyes blur faces now. I could not name the officer before you.
No. I sleep beautifully. My husband forbids me working at night.
Forgetfulness. Yesterday I could not recall my own block number.
I have recorded every resident in this district. Is that not a comfort?
The last officer here asked about the blast. He was not here long.
The list is shorter now. Those people did not listen. Exactly to plan.
I wrote your name down! Do not worry. A list of the faithful. For now.
Whatever the blast was, it was permitted. That is what makes it beautiful.
Doubt spreads faster than any sickness. I report both. Happily!
